title: Stop bee blind check panicking on a citation that starts with a curly quote
action:
FIX-FIRST, and read the scope note: this is NOT another rung on the sentence-boundary rule. That rule SURVIVED its third judge round — 36 probes, and everything that still passes falls inside a limit the comment already names. This is a different defect class: a panic.

THE DEFECT. `quote_resolves` (blind/mod.rs:796, :810) advances its retry cursor by one BYTE — `from = start + 1` — and then slices the `&str`. When the citation's first character is MULTIBYTE and its first occurrence fails the boundary check, the slice lands mid-character and the process panics instead of returning a refusal.

The judge's reproduction, verbatim:
  proposal: He said “cache the token on the worker side” loudly today.
  citation: “cache the token on the worker side
  It clears both floors (35 chars, 7 words), then panics with `byte index 9 is not a char boundary; it is inside '“' (bytes 8..11 of string)`.
An em dash does the same: proposal `x — cache the token on the worker side y.` cited as `— cache the token on the worker side y`.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CRASH. `normalize` (:647-661) deliberately PRESERVES non-ASCII, so the comment at :787-788 claiming the scan is over ASCII bytes is FALSE — fix that line too. A curly quote or an em dash is what you get from any prose copied out of a rendered document, which is exactly where a lane proposal comes from. So `bee blind check` aborts on ordinary input rather than answering, and a verb whose whole job is to refuse dishonest evidence instead dies without a verdict.

WHAT TO DO.
1. Probes FIRST, run red before the fix: the curly-quote reproduction and the em-dash one, both verbatim from above. A panicking test fails loudly, so assert the REFUSAL these must produce, not the panic.
2. Fix the cursor. Advance to the next CHARACTER boundary, never a raw byte — walk `char_indices`, or step by the matched character's `len_utf8`. Audit every other slice and index in `quote_resolves`, `citation_quote`, `is_sentence_end` and `is_enumerator` for the same assumption while you are in there, and say in your report which ones you checked.
3. Correct the :787-788 comment: the scan is over UTF-8 bytes and `normalize` preserves non-ASCII, so byte indexing here must be char-boundary safe.
4. Add one probe with a multibyte character in the MIDDLE of both proposal and citation, and one where the citation is entirely non-ASCII, so the fix is proven past the two reported strings rather than only against them.
5. All 51 existing `verbs::blind` tests stay green and none is edited.

PROHIBITIONS. Do not make `normalize` strip or fold non-ASCII to dodge this — that would silently rewrite the bytes a citation is checked against, which is the whole point of the check. Do not weaken the floors, the per-lane scoping, the boundary rule or any other check. Do not touch the framing probe.

The em-dash citation does the same, pinned by its own probe

normalize still preserves non-ASCII — the fix is in the cursor, never in the normalizer
